tour.overview:
Milan is Italy's capital of business and fashion, but it also holds one of the most famous paintings in the world. Between 1495 and 1498, Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper on the wall of the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie, capturing the moment Christ announces that one of the apostles will betray him. The church and the painting have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980. An hour north, Lake Como fills a deep valley shaped like an upside-down Y between wooded mountains, its shores lined with villages and the gardens of grand villas.

This private day combines both. In the morning your guide shows you the Last Supper with reserved tickets, which sell out months ahead, then Milan's cathedral and the Galleria. Your driver takes you to Bellagio on the lake, where you walk the lanes and the waterfront, then cross by ferry to Varenna for lunch and a stroll among its pastel houses, before driving back to Milan.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Milan
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver; public ferry on the lake
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km, with some steep lanes in Bellagio and Varenna

WHAT YOU SEE
• Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper in Santa Maria delle Grazie.
• Milan Cathedral (Duomo) and its square.
• The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II and La Scala opera house (outside).
• Bellagio and its waterfront.
• The ferry across Lake Como.
• Varenna and its lakeside walk.

WHY THIS WORKS
The Last Supper allows only small groups for 15 minutes at a time, and tickets are very hard to find; we secure them with your booking and build the day around your slot.

WHO IT SUITS
Art lovers, couples and anyone in Milan for a few days who wants both the city's treasure and the lake.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer more time on the lake, ask us for a full day on Lake Como with a private boat and a visit to Villa del Balbianello or Villa Carlotta.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Last Supper tickets are personal and must be booked well in advance: send your request as early as you can, and we will confirm only once the tickets are secured. The Last Supper is closed on Mondays. The Duomo requires covered shoulders and knees.

days.name: Leonardo's Last Supper, Milan Cathedral and the Galleria, Bellagio, the ferry to Varenna and lunch on Lake Como
days.description:
What to expect: Milan's great treasures and the most elegant of the Italian lakes in one day, with a licensed guide, private car, reserved tickets, ferry and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:00. Your guide meets you at Santa Maria delle Grazie, a Renaissance church whose dome and choir were designed by Bramante. Before your timed slot, you learn the story of the painting: Leonardo worked slowly, in tempera and oil on dry plaster rather than in fresco, so that he could change and perfect it, and the paint began to flake within his lifetime. The refectory survived a bomb in 1943 that destroyed the roof, and a restoration finished in 1999 brought back colours hidden for centuries. Inside, with only a small group, you have 15 minutes face to face with the apostles reacting to Christ's words, each in his own way.

You drive to the centre to see the Duomo, begun in 1386 and finished only in the 20th century, with its forest of 135 spires and some 3,400 statues; inside, the stained-glass windows are among the largest in the world. You walk through the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the glass-roofed arcade of 1877 where Milanese spin on the mosaic bull for luck, to the square of La Scala opera house.

Your driver then takes you north to Lake Como, about 1 hour 15 minutes away. In Bellagio, on the point where the lake's three branches meet, you walk the steep stepped lanes and the waterfront promenade lined with oleanders. A public ferry takes you across the water in about 15 minutes to Varenna, a village of pastel houses where you have lunch on a terrace above the lake – risotto with perch, the local fish, or polenta and Alpine cheeses. After a stroll on the lakeside walkway, your driver meets you in Varenna and takes you back to your hotel in Milan at about 18:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:30 – Santa Maria delle Grazie and the Last Supper (timed slot).
09:30 – Milan Cathedral (about 1 hour).
10:45 – Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II and La Scala.
11:15 – Drive to Lake Como.
12:30 – Bellagio.
13:30 – Ferry to Varenna.
13:45 – Lunch in Varenna and lakeside walk.
16:15 – Drive back to Milan.
18:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Last Supper time slot fixes the order of the day; if the only available slot is in the afternoon, we visit the lake first.
• The Duomo rooftop terraces can be added, by lift or stairs.
• A private boat on the lake, instead of the public ferry, can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Last Supper and Duomo tickets, ferry, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Duomo rooftop terraces, villa gardens on the lake, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are Last Supper tickets guaranteed?
faq.answer: Tickets are released in limited numbers and sell out fast, so we confirm your tour only once we have secured them. The earlier you send your request, the better your chances.

faq.question: How long can we see the Last Supper?
faq.answer: Visits last 15 minutes in small groups, a rule set to protect the painting. Your guide explains the work beforehand so you can use every minute to look.

faq.question: On which days is the tour not possible?
faq.answer: The Last Supper is closed on Mondays. On Mondays we can offer Milan's other treasures and Lake Como instead.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Last Supper and Milan Cathedral, plus the ferry from Bellagio to Varenna. The cathedral terraces and lakeside villas can be added.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a lakeside restaurant. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it a long day?
faq.answer: About 10 hours, with roughly 2 hours 30 minutes of driving in total on motorways and lake roads. The car is comfortable, and you can rest on the ferry.

faq.question: Can we visit George Clooney's village?
faq.answer: Laglio is on the western shore, on the way to Bellagio by the lake road; your driver can point it out. The villa itself is private.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the ferry, the cathedral's gargoyles and the lake. Child seats are provided free of charge on request. Children of all ages are admitted to the Last Supper.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Last Supper and the Duomo are accessible, but Bellagio and Varenna have steep, stepped lanes. Tell us your needs and we will adapt the lake part.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Clothes covering shoulders and knees for the Duomo and the church, comfortable shoes, and a light jacket for the ferry.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October, when the lake gardens are in flower and the ferries run often. In winter many lakeside restaurants close and the ferries are fewer.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because Last Supper tickets are non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
